It supports two modes: 25 26 - **Incremental.** Opens a single mechanical PR that opts every route out of validation, then ships each feature as a follow-up PR. This automates the [Adopting incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) flow below. 27 - **Direct.** Adopts every route in place on one branch. 28 29 Install the skill: 30 31 ```bash filename="Terminal" 32 npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-cache-components-adoption 33 ``` 34 35 Then give the agent this prompt: 36 37 ```prompt 38 Adopt Cache Components in this project using the next-cache-components-adoption skill. 39 ``` 40 41 ## Or migrate by hand 42 43 Migrating an existing app by hand follows a few steps, in order: 44 45 1. [Enable Cache Components](#enable-cache-components) in `next.config.ts`. 46 2. Decide your approach: convert every route now, or [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) by [opting routes out of validation](#opting-out-of-validation) first and converting one at a time. 47 3. [Follow the validation errors and insights](#following-validation) it surfaces, replacing each route segment config with its Cache Components equivalent and caching uncached data with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or wrapping runtime data in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). If you're on Next.js 15 or earlier, upgrade first by following the [version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16). It does not force the route to be dynamic, so a genuinely prerenderable route still ships a static shell. It also does not clear synchronous IO build errors: calls like `new Date()`, `Math.random()`, and `crypto.randomUUID()` still fail the prerender. See [Adopting incrementally](#adopting-incrementally). 87 88 ## Adopting incrementally 89 90 You don't have to migrate every route at once. `instant = false` lets you get the whole app building and running first, then convert routes one at a time: 91 92 1. **Enable the flag and migrate each route segment config.** Follow the relevant sections below for [`dynamic = "force-dynamic"`](#dynamic--force-dynamic), [`dynamic = "force-static"`](#dynamic--force-static), [`dynamic = "error"`](#dynamic--error), [`revalidate`](#revalidate), and [`fetchCache`](#fetchcache). For routes with dynamic params, also follow the [`generateStaticParams`](#generatestaticparams-and-dynamicparams) guidance. 86 	
87 	### Cache profile properties
88 	
89 	Cache profiles control caching behavior through three timing properties:
90 	
91 	- **[`stale`](#stale)**: How long the client can use cached data without checking the server
92 	- **[`revalidate`](#revalidate)**: After this time, the next request will trigger a background refresh
93 	- **[`expire`](#expire)**: After this time with no requests, the next one waits for fresh content
94 	
95 	#### `stale`
96 	
97 	**Client-side:** How long the client can use cached data without checking the server.
98 	
99 	During this time, the client-side router displays cached content immediately without any network request. After this period expires, the router must check with the server on the next navigation or request. This provides instant page loads from the client cache, but data may be outdated.
100	
101	- If omitted, defaults to the `default` profile's `stale` value (5 minutes, see [`staleTimes`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/staleTimes))
102	- Also determines whether the content can be part of the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). See [Prerendering behavior](#prerendering-behavior).
103	
104	```tsx
105	cacheLife({ stale: 300 }) // 5 minutes
106	```
107	
108	#### `revalidate`
109	
110	How often the server regenerates cached content in the background.
111	
112	- When a request arrives after this period, the server:
113	  1. Serves the cached version immediately (if available)
114	  2. Regenerates content in the background
115	  3. Updates the cache with fresh content
116	- Similar to [Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR)](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration)
117	- If omitted, defaults to the `default` profile's `revalidate` value (15 minutes)
118	
119	```tsx
120	cacheLife({ revalidate: 900 }) // 15 minutes
121	```
122

124	
125	Maximum time before the server must regenerate cached content.

133	```

143	| `minutes`   | Frequently updated content             | 5 minutes  | 1 minute     | 1 hour   |
144	| `hours`     | Content updated multiple times per day | 5 minutes  | 1 hour       | 1 day    |
145	| `days`      | Content updated daily                  | 5 minutes  | 1 day        | 1 week   |
146	| `weeks`     | Content updated weekly                 | 5 minutes  | 1 week       | 30 days  |
147	| `max`       | Stable content that rarely changes     | 5 minutes  | 30 days      | 1 year   |

150	
151	The preset profiles map to familiar time periods (`seconds`, `minutes`, `hours`, `days`, `weeks`), alongside `default` and `max`. You can use these as they are, or redefine any of them, including `default` and `max`, in `next.config.ts`. The built-in names keep working with editor autocomplete.

12	Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.
13	
14	## Usage
15	
16	To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file:
17	
18	```ts filename="next.config.ts"

20	
21	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
22	  cacheComponents: true,
23	}
24	
25	export default nextConfig
26	```
27	
28	> **Good to know**: Cache Components requires the Node.js runtime. Migrate any routes that set the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'` export, and note that other server-side JavaScript runtimes are not guaranteed to work. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components#runtime--edge).
29	
30	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, you can use the following cache functions and configurations:
31	
32	- The [`use cache` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache)
33	- The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache`
34	- The [`cacheTag` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag)
35	
36	> **Good to know**: If you used `experimental.useCache` or `experimental.dynamicIO`, migrate using the [Version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). To migrate route segment configs and other caching patterns, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components).
37	
38	Additionally, `cacheComponents` implements **[Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prerendering-ppr)** as the default behavior in the App Router. This means the `experimental.ppr` configuration flag and the `experimental_ppr` route segment configuration are no longer necessary and have been removed.
39	
40	Read [Prerendering](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) for how the static shell and streaming fit together.
41	
42	> **Good to know**: If you used experimental PPR in Next.js 15, refer to the [Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#partial-prerendering-ppr) section of the Version 16 upgrade guide when migrating.
43	
44	## Navigation with Activity
45	
46	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, Next.js uses React's [`<Activity>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity) component to preserve component state during client-side navigation.
47	
48	Rather than unmounting the previous route when you navigate away, Next.js sets the Activity mode to [`"hidden"`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity#activity). This means:

50	- Component state is preserved when navigating between routes
51	- When you navigate back, the previous route reappears with its state intact
52	- Effects are cleaned up when a route is hidden, and recreated when it becomes visible again
53	
54	This behavior improves the navigation experience by maintaining UI state (form inputs, or expanded sections) when users navigate back and forth between routes.
55

57

59

63	| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
64	| 16.0.0  | `cacheComponents` introduced. This flag controls the `ppr`, `useCache`, and `dynamicIO` flags as a single, unified configuration. |

17 	The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable.
